items.change: Borrow nodes, cache generated SQL and bigrams, and index descendant-leaf ranges.
Reuse bottom-up type results and static function mappings; prepare source schemas once per projection list.
Index output lookups and omit unused intermediate query copies in the private OpenLineage resolver.
Use borrowed source views for nullability analysis and remove a redundant lateral-source clone. Public owned Scope construction remains unchanged.
Share immutable AST storage for child views, walks, and searches while preserving independent builder results.
Deserialize valid AST JSON directly; retain the legacy compatibility and error fallback.

Avoid rebuilding containers in read-only traversal and stop findFirst immediately. Retain the JSON bridge with the faster core decoder: the structured bridge prototype was about 35% slower in the same-build comparison.
Skip inapplicable built-in passes, including boolean rewrites over scalar-only nested queries. Preserve pass order and custom callbacks.
Use path-free AST guard traversal and the borrowed parser-token path for formatting.

Keep source offsets instead of per-token Arc handles, compact empty comment slots, and borrow unchanged Unicode text during parsing. Retain the original public Unicode tokenizer cursor after detecting a regression.
Compared wasm-opt -Oz and -O3 on the same Rust artifact. Retain -Oz: -O3 produced no consistent runtime win and increased bundle size.

Run SQL operations and WASM startup in a dedicated Web Worker; queue requests during asynchronous initialization, mount tabs on first visit, ignore stale responses, and reuse lineage results to collect source tables.

notes: Synthetic workloads; speedups apply to the named workload and size, not every query.
The main before/after comparison uses the fixed performance profile, not the production release profiles.
WASM init timings are single observations and are not evidence of a startup-speed improvement.
The public owned Scope API still requires owned ASTs; this work does not remove all scope-construction cloning.
The playground retains its existing transpile-then-format behavior to preserve displayed SQL.
Python child views keep the root AST alive until the last view is released; copy() continues to create an independent AST.
The main performance-profile WASM artifact grew from 46,426,693 to 50,441,180 bytes (+8.65%); gzip grew from 7,909,337 to 8,871,330 bytes (+12.16%). Production release size has not been measured.
findFirst matching the root is a best-case early-exit microbenchmark. The nested Fabric case exposes the previous repeated-recursion behavior; neither is an overall throughput estimate.
Three Rust test expectations already disagree with baseline output. Final output still matches that baseline; see baseline-test-failures.json.
